question: Can we prescribe a genuinely 3-D, connected, periodic auxetic cell that the existing OpenPFC 3-D homogenizer evaluates as nu<0?

geometry.name: reentrant-3d
geometry.primary_source: Yang, L., Harrysson, O., West, H. & Cormier, D., Int. J. Solids Struct. 69-70 (2015) 475-490
geometry.also: Evans, K. E., Nkansah, M. A. & Hutchinson, I. J., Acta Metall. Mater. 42 (1994) 1289-1294 (inverted honeycomb)
geometry.mechanism: Re-entrant V-struts in xz and yz with four-fold patterning about vertical pillars (Gibson-Robert). Small-strain bending in the literature, not contact/buckling.
geometry.expected_auxetic_directions: Yang: NPR in all three principal directions; x and y equivalent; z distinguished
geometry.published_regime: small-deflection Timoshenko and large-deflection beam models plus AM experiments

parameters_frozen_before_poisson.squares: all four 0.5-squares (one representation correction from checkerboard)

representation_correction.first_occupancy: checkerboard two squares; connected; perc xyz; all nu>0 (job 22157477)
representation_correction.correction: add V-struts on the remaining two 0.5-squares so every bay is re-entrant
representation_correction.second_occupancy: job 22157558; still connected, perc xyz, all nu>0

material.note: Same ersatz as the qualified 2-D rotating-square seed; not tuned to force nu<0.

interpretation: After one representation correction (all four re-entrant bays), the voxel cell is 3-D, one solid component, perc xyz, SPD, and all six compliance Poisson ratios are positive at 32^3 and 64^3 (nu_xy≈+0.22, nu_zx≈+0.31). PR #34 already showed the 3-D homogenizer can produce nu_xy<0, so this is not a Voigt/compliance bug. Remaining caveats vs Yang 2015: through-going half-lattice pillars are not finite-H verticals, and t/L≈0.17 is a stubby continuum strut not a slender Timoshenko beam. One correction used; no further tuning. Do not start inverse design.
